newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond futures seen forming base.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bond futures seen forming base.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures may be basing out after a fairly long downtrend, technical analysts said.

T-bond futures looked set to end higher on the week after eight straight down weeks since mid-February, they noted. June T-bonds, which started Monday at 106-20/32, stood at 107-31/32 in late morning trade, marginally firmer on the day.
"It looks like bonds have broken out of a small base and I anticipate some followthrough in the coming weeks," said Jim Bohan, senior financial futures strategist at Merrill Lynch Capital Markets.
Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage, said the weekly stochastic was starting to turn up at deeply oversold levels that had been reached only four times in the last 15 years.
"Ultimately, this is going to be a wonderful turning point that does not repeat frequently," he said.

The daily stochastic, which had seen a few failed bullish divergences, was proceeding with a more convincing upmove, he added. Bullish divergences occur when percent-K and D values of stochastics make higher lows as bond prices pull back.
He said the daily would inevitably lose steam fairly soon and that would be when the market faces the big test.
"We'll have to get refreshed and see if the next downturn puts us in a bullish divergence and whether in fact the weekly would lock in and form a base," Grauer said.
He added that the monthly stochastic was within oversold areas and was likely to turn upward following a basing in the weekly.
Bohan at Merrill Lynch said the market should have a positive bias as long as support levels near 107 in the June contract held.
"Sentiment numbers are showing a great deal of bearishness and yet it looks like momentum has turned up," he said.

"It's not powerful, but when you consider how the bearishness had grown in the past couple of weeks and the bonds haven't really lost any ground, I think it's a pretty good situation right now," he noted.
The market is likely soon to re-focus on the Federal Reserve's monetary policy as the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting approaches.

While fears of a series of interest rate hikes to follow the March tightening may keep the market jittery, Grauer said early rate hikes in big increments would be more positive for bonds than a prolonged, sequential rise as in 1994.
